headline: EU releases forced labour guidance and sets 2026 sustainability reporting priorities
summary: The European Commission published official implementation guidelines for the Forced Labour Regulation. ESMA established its 2026 enforcement priorities for CSRD reporting, emphasizing double materiality. Additionally, reports indicate new limits on supplier sustainability data requests.

items.title: Commission publishes official EU Forced Labour Regulation guidelines
items.what: The European Commission published official guidelines for implementing the EU Forced Labour Regulation.
items.meaning: Essential for reviewing supply chain due diligence and risk assessment processes across your Chinese manufacturing suppliers.
items.action: Review supplier auditing protocols against the new guidelines to ensure supply chain compliance.

sources.title: Update on the EU Forced Labour Regulation: The European Commission's Guidelines Have Been Published

items.title: ESMA sets 2026 enforcement priorities for CSRD sustainability reporting
items.what: ESMA and national regulators published 2026 sustainability reporting priorities, focusing heavily on double materiality and connected information.
items.meaning: Prepares your business for mandatory CSRD reporting starting FY2027, highlighting the need for robust double materiality assessments.
items.action: Align upcoming FY2027 ESG data collection with ESMA double materiality guidance.

sources.title: EU Sustainability reporting – ESMA sets 2026 common enforcement priorities – materiality and providing connected information remain firmly in focus
Preparing upcoming sustainability statements: the AMF draws listed companies’ attention to ESMA’s 2026 recommendations

items.title: Reported limits introduced on sustainability data requests from suppliers
items.what: Media reported that proposed EU rules introduce limits allowing suppliers with up to 1,000 staff to decline excessive data requests.
items.meaning: May affect how you collect primary sustainability data from mid-sized Chinese tool and component suppliers.
items.action: Streamline supplier questionnaires to focus only on essential, standardised ESG datapoints.

sources.title: Brussels Sets a Data Ceiling: Suppliers With Up to 1,000 Staff Can Now Refuse Extra Sustainability R

items.title: EU clarifies and narrows product scopes under deforestation regulation
items.what: Reports indicate the EU has clarified and narrowed EUDR rules and product scopes affecting rubber and timber-derived goods.
items.meaning: Relevant if your garden equipment or power tools incorporate rubber components, wood packaging, or timber handles.
items.action: Check affected component supply chains against updated EUDR product scope definitions.

sources.title: EU Narrows and Clarifies Deforestation Rules Affecting Furniture, Rubber and Other Goods

items.title: PEFC updates certification rules to align with EU green claims directive
items.what: PEFC amended its trademark and certification rules to align with the EU Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive.
items.meaning: Impacts environmental claims on product packaging and timber handles certified under PEFC schemes.
items.action: Verify that marketing claims using PEFC labels comply with updated rules.

sources.title: PEFC amends trademark rules to align with EU EmpCo requirements
